result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned hand-written source and checked-in application configuration for passwords, credentials, embedded crypto keys, explicit ACL assignments and logging. Default LocalDB connection string contains no password; environment-provided ConnectionString contents were not read. No secret values reproduced. Missing endpoint authentication and directory browsing are configuration concerns, but do not alone prove an explicit incorrect ACL assignment (CWE-732). Deployment ACLs, external secret stores and infrastructure audit logging were not examined. Static review only.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem and RemoveCatalogItem modify persistent catalog data and call SaveChanges without recording actor, operation, target or outcome. No application audit logger or configured WCF audit behavior was found. Consequently security-relevant changes cannot be attributed using application audit records. External IIS/database monitoring might exist but was not provided and cannot be inferred.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
